sources.note: Read through a summarizing fetch on 2026-11-17. Relevant text: the Session Time Limits policies 'Set time limit for disconnected sessions', 'Set time limit for active but idle Remote Desktop Services sessions', 'Set time limit for active Remote Desktop Services sessions' and 'End Session when time limits are reached', under Computer Configuration > Administrative Templates > Windows Components > Remote Desktop Services > Remote Desktop Session Host > Session Time Limits. The page does not cover Intune or what happens at the limit; that a disconnected session is ended (unsaved work lost) at its limit, and that the CIS Intune Windows 11 Level 2 benchmark item 18.10.58.3.10.2 sets the disconnected limit to 1 minute (title seen in a search result from tenable.com), are to verify.

brief.situation: You are the AVD administrator at Merrow Insurance. Field adjusters use the host pool hp-field from tablets on cellular networks. Yesterday the security team assigned a hardening baseline to all AVD session hosts through Intune. Since this morning adjusters say that whenever the signal drops for a moment, they reconnect to a fresh desktop and the claim they were writing is gone. A hail storm surge starts at 10:30, when 120 adjusters go out.
handover: The baseline profile is 'Win11 L2 hardening', owned by the security team, assigned to the AVD-Hosts device group.
Before yesterday, hp-field hosts had no session time limits set.
howItWorks: The terminal shows each command's output; the diagram shows the Intune baseline, the session hosts' time limits and the adjusters' sessions.
Each command takes a minute or two; the clock moves only when you act or wait.
When you close, you write the record and explain your reasoning.

writeup.question: For the record: why adjusters lost their sessions, what you changed with whom, and how it stays right.

parts.label: Why
parts.criteria: Connects the logoffs to the limit.
parts.modelAnswer: Events showed each disconnected session logged off a minute later. The hosts had MaxDisconnectionTime of one minute from yesterday's Intune hardening profile (a desktop benchmark item), and cellular clients drop for seconds many times a day.

parts.label: Change
parts.criteria: Overrides one setting, with the owner.
parts.modelAnswer: With the security team's approval: an AVD policy with a 4-hour disconnected limit and a 2-hour idle limit, and the baseline item excluded for AVD hosts. Unassigning the profile would have removed all the hardening.

parts.label: Stays right
parts.modelAnswer: The exception is in the baseline's notes and an alert fires on logoffs shortly after disconnects.

expertPath.text: Logoff one minute after disconnect; MaxDisconnectionTime 1 minute; set by yesterday's hardening profile; cellular drops.

unhardened.headline: One setting, not the baseline
unhardened.body: Only the disconnected-session limit was wrong for AVD. Override that one setting for the AVD hosts with the security team; keep the rest.

surgeLost.headline: A desktop benchmark item on a remote desktop
surgeLost.body: On a session host, the disconnected-session limit decides whether a user who drops can come back. One minute is shorter than a cellular blip lasts.

limitsSet.headline: Good: session limits that fit the users
limitsSet.body: You read why sessions ended, traced the setting to the baseline, set AVD-appropriate limits for the hosts with the security team, tested a reconnect, and recorded the exception.

scoring.modelReasoning: Each disconnected session is logged off a minute later because yesterday's hardening profile set a one-minute disconnected-session limit, and cellular clients drop briefly all the time. Agree AVD-appropriate limits with the security team, override just that item for the AVD hosts, and test a reconnect. Unassigning the whole profile removes all hardening; a different transport does not change the limit. Record the exception and watch for the pattern.
